messages:
maya: FYI, noticed a recurring latency spike on edge-rack-7 after the nightly backfill window. GPU stalls + packet drops in dmesg. Seems correlated with allocations that backfill into fractional dedicated slices.
jon: Can you paste the p99 / p50 for that timeframe? also which tenant(s) got backfilled?
maya: p50 ~18ms, p95 ~120ms, p99 spikes to 450ms for inference paths. Backfill time around 02:10 UTC. Tenants: @rafa-service and a couple of low-priority PLG demos.
lee: is this the warm-pool backfill we enabled last month? we did change the soft-affinity thresholds to 60% before we said 70%.
anika: quick thought — if fractional slices are sharing NVLINK / PCIe lanes with dedicated tenants, we could see direct contention leaking into the dedicated queue. Any kernel IRQ churn or NIC queue saturation?
maya: yeah kernel shows a burst of irq and `mlx5` tx drops. dmesg snippet: ```
[02:10:12] mlx5_core error: TX queue 3 overflow
[02:10:12] net_ratelimit: 120 callbacks suppressed
[02:10:13] GPU stall detected: ctxsw timeout
```
jon: that log + p99 suggests noisy neighbors at the NIC/PCIe path, not just CPU. We should prevent backfill into racks where dedicated slices exist until we have egress shaping.
rafa: oof, that's my demo tenant. Noticed a few user complaints this morning. Are we suggesting we block backfill by default or add a penalty score so backfill avoids racks with ded pools?
lee: penalty score seems safer. Proposal: increase backfill cost if a rack has >=1 dedicated slice allocated. Cost function change in allocator: `cost += rack.dedicated_count * BACKFILL_PENALTY` where BACKFILL_PENALTY=1000 for now. That should steer backfill away without hard blocking.
anika: also suggest a temporary mitigation: add NIC TX shaping on the host for the low-priority slice: `tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root tbf rate 300mbit burst 32k` — keep it until we have egress QoS in the proxy.
maya: can someone run `kubectl top pod` + `sar` on host `edge-rack-7-n1`? I'm on-call but juggling another incident.
jon: grabbing it now. running: `ssh ops@edge-rack-7-n1 'sar -n DEV 1 3; nvidia-smi dmon -s u'`
jon: sar shows tx errs burst at 02:10 and `nvidia-smi dmon` shows power jitter concurrent with the NIC burst.
rafa: cost question — if we make backfill avoid racks with dedicated slices, we may increase cold start rate elsewhere and inflate costs. need to model: is the extra idle time > cost of noisy neighbor incidents?
lee: short calc: noisy incident cost ~4 hours of SLAs impacted per week * mitigation ops time ≈ $2k/week for high-impact tenants. Backfill avoidance increases warm-pool misses ~3% -> ~+$800/week. net win to avoid. rough numbers, need finance eyeballs.
anika: I'll file a short runbook: 1) set BACKFILL_PENALTY=1000 in allocator config (canary eu-west), 2) enable host tc shaping for low-priority slices on edge racks, 3) add probe to detect pci/irq spikes and temporarily quarantine backfill for 30m.
maya: tagging @jon @lee to coordinate rollout. ops-bot: create incident ticket for the network+gpu regression and link logs.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3287 — "edge-rack-7 backfill -> NIC/PCIe contention causing gpu stalls". Pager: eng-infra, oncall-maya.
jon: I'll roll the allocator change to canary tonight 01:00 UTC and monitor the warm-pool miss rate. Will update thread once canary is stable.
maya: thanks. if you need me to flip shaping on any host ping me.
rafa: i'll throttle my demos for tonight to reduce blast radius. appreciate the quick coordination. :heart:
lee: if canary looks good we should make BACKFILL_PENALTY configurable per-region — apac racks are tighter.
maya: agreed. leaving notes in the incident and tagging finance for cost validation.
